text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool surge detected in eu-west-1 (pool-eu-west-1). Error rate spike and request drops for some customers. Affected customers: Acme Inc., BetaCorp. Incident ID: INC-2026-0421-77. Auto-scaling not keeping up. Paging on-call.

jordan_oncall: I'm on it. Thanks bot. Quick ask: can we enable burst capacity and apply per-customer throttles while we stabilize?

maria: taking the action. will run burst toggle + temporary rate caps.

ashok: heads-up — enabling burst will spin up reserved nodes, cost jump possible. prefer targeted per-customer caps first if that buys time.

lina_sre: cluster checks: ``pool_eu_west_1: util=92% cpu/gpu, queue_depth=820, 95p_latency=420ms, drop_rate=6.8%``. Autoscaler backoff seen at 30s, didn't provision additional nodes.

jordan_oncall: thanks Lina. Maria, do caps first, then burst if needed. Prioritize Acme (largest QPS) then BetaCorp. Post exact commands you run.

maria: applying caps to Acme and BetaCorp now.

maria: ```
# temporary throttle rules
redwoodctl rate set --customer Acme --qps 5 --duration 15m --reason "INC-2026-0421-77 emergency throttle"
redwoodctl rate set --customer BetaCorp --qps 3 --duration 15m --reason "INC-2026-0421-77 emergency throttle"
```

maria: caps applied — control plane ACK: Acme qps=5, BetaCorp qps=3. Observability dashboard shows immediate drop in incoming QPS for both. :white_check_mark:

ashok: good. Monitor tail latency — sometimes throttles push retries from clients and increase burstiness.

jordan_oncall: Maria, please toggle burst if drops don't go below 1% in 10m.

lina_sre: running a one-off autoscale trigger to force capacity increase while we watch. ``redwoodctl autoscale trigger --pool pool-eu-west-1 --reason "emergency provision"`` output: "scale job queued, target +4 nodes".

maria: burst toggle now (if needed):
```bash
redwoodctl dedicated toggle-burst --pool pool-eu-west-1 --enable --duration 30m
# response: "burst-enabled pool-eu-west-1, provision jobs started"
```

maria: executed toggle-burst. Provisioning logs show nodes allocating. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lina_sre: metrics update 3m after actions: util=78%, queue_depth=210, 95p_latency=190ms, drop_rate=0.9%. Looks like combined caps+burst helped.

jordan_oncall: nice. Keep monitoring. Sam, can you draft a short customer update for Acme & BetaCorp ops? Keep it minimal: we're mitigating, temporary throttles, no data loss.

sam_support: draft: "Hi — we saw a brief surge affecting request rates in eu-west-1. We've applied temporary throttles and enabled burst capacity to stabilize traffic. Expected perf to return to normal within 30 minutes. No data loss. Contact support if you see issues." Want me to send? @jordan_oncall

jordan_oncall: send the note, include incident ID. Good to CC account teams.

maria: monitoring continues. Post-action logs from provision: 4 new nodes green and CPU/GPU ready. ``nodes_added=4, time=180s``.

ashok: please schedule a follow-up to discuss autoscaler tuning; backoff thresholds are too aggressive for short bursts. Might want a faster short-term scale path.

jordan_oncall: Agreed. Add to the postmortem. For now, mitigation success — drop_rate under 1% and key customers stable. I'll hand this to ops for post-incident analysis in ~2h.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421-77: Mitigation applied (temporary throttles + burst enabled). Monitoring for 30m.

maria: closing active mitigations in 30m if metrics stay steady. Leaving monitoring channel open.

sam_support: sent customer notes to Acme and BetaCorp. Both acknowledged. :thumbsup:

jordan_oncall: thanks everyone. Add remediation: revisit autoscaler target policy, add tier-aware emergency throttle automation, and document burst cost opt-in. Will open follow-up ticket. :white_check_mark:
